summary: Neo comes up behind Cypher at the operator's chair on the main deck, startling him. Cypher explains that the screens show the Matrix in encoded form because there is too much information to decode, though the brain learns to translate it. He offers Neo a drink and pours clear alcohol from a plastic jug. They toast, and Cypher jokes that he keeps wishing he had taken the blue pill. Neo nearly chokes on the shot. Cypher then asks whether Morpheus told Neo why he is here; when Neo confirms he is there to save the world, Cypher calls it a mindjob and reveals this is not the first time Morpheus thought he had found the One. He says there have been five since he arrived, all dead, killed because Morpheus got them to believe in bullshit and each took on an Agent and died. He advises Neo to run if he ever sees an Agent. Neo thanks him for the drink and heads for the ladder as Cypher wishes him sweet dreams.

what_changes.before: Unsure and quietly awed, Neo is new to the ship's view of the Matrix and to his own role.
what_changes.after: Neo learns that Morpheus has believed he found the One five times before and that all five died taking on an Agent, reframing his destiny as part of a deadly pattern.
what_changes.evidence: this ain't the first time Morpheus thought he found the One. ... Five. Since I've been here. ... Dead. All dead. ... I watched each of them take on an Agent and I watched each of them die.

what_changes.before: Sober and curious, approaching the screens with wonder.
what_changes.after: Drunk and physically rattled, red-faced and coughing after two shots of Dozer's liquor.
what_changes.evidence: Neo does the same and it almost kills him. ... Red-faced, Neo finally stops coughing. Cypher pours him another. ... Neo gulps down another shot.

what_changes.before: Playing the welcoming crewmate, sharing a drink and small talk.
what_changes.after: He quietly undermines Morpheus, confessing his own regret and painting Morpheus as someone who gets men killed with false belief.
what_changes.evidence: Why, oh why, didn't I take that blue pill? ... Morpheus. He got them all amped up believing in bullshit. I watched each of them take on an Agent and I watched each of them die.

event_hint.one_line: Over a late-night drink on the main deck, Cypher disillusionment-seeds Neo about Morpheus's prophecy.

objects_that_matter: the screens showing the encoded Matrix
a plastic jug of clear alcohol
uncertain: Whether Cypher intends to betray the crew outright or is only venting disillusionment.
How drunk Neo actually becomes or whether he takes Cypher's warnings to heart.

minds.wants: To recruit Neo — not to the cause, but into his private disillusionment. He wants a co-conspirator in doubt, someone who will nod along while he says what no one else on the ship is allowed to say, so that his own regret stops being a solitary, disloyal secret and becomes shared common sense.
minds.feels: Deep, settled resentment toward Morpheus and the prophecy, layered over genuine terror of the Agents he has watched kill five men. The wish he voices — that he'd taken the blue pill — is not a joke to him; it is the real center of gravity of his life, and being trapped on a cold ship after the Sentinel scare (sc-070–072) has sharpened it into something bitter enough to finally leak.
minds.shows: The easy, back-slapping crewmate: he startles theatrically, explains the screens with worldly charm ('blonde, brunette, and redhead'), pours the drink, and frames everything as a joke ('Why, oh why, didn't I take that blue pill?'). Even the subversion of Morpheus is delivered as gossip, not a manifesto — 'don't tell him I told you this' keeps it inside the register of confiding camaraderie.
minds.basis: The staged 'Whoa! you scared me' opening establishes a chummy tone he then uses as cover; he explicitly says he's been thinking the blue-pill thought 'ever since I got here,' then steers the conversation himself toward Morpheus ('Did he happen to tell you why... why you're here?'), reframes 'save the world' as 'What a mindjob,' and reveals the five dead candidates while attributing their deaths to Morpheus getting them 'amped up believing in bullshit.' The physical staging — pouring Neo drink after drink — gives the seduction a chemical engine.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a malleable, awed newcomer who can be turned against Morpheus's certainty if given the 'inside' version — that Neo, like him, is really just scared and will be flattered to be let in on the secret.
believes_about.wrong_because: He reads Neo's wide-eyed staring at the screens and his unsure looks as the same doubt he feels in himself, but Neo's awe is genuine curiosity and nascent commitment, not disillusionment; Neo takes the warning to heart as caution, not as permission to betray. Cypher mistakes a shared drink for a shared soul, which is exactly why his later betrayal (ev-023) will be so catastrophic — he never actually knew the man he was trying to recruit.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a dangerous fanatic who gets men killed by selling them a lie, and that the prophecy is mere ego-sustaining fantasy.
believes_about.wrong_because: This reading is not contradicted within the scene, but it is incomplete: it flattens Morpheus's faith into con-artistry. The coming Oracle scene (ev-021) and the fact that Neo does not, in fact, die suggest the prophecy is not the pure 'bullshit' Cypher insists it is — Cypher's certainty that he sees the whole truth is itself the blind spot.

minds.wants: To belong — to be one of the crew, to understand this world and his place in it, and to measure himself against the role ('save the world') he's just been handed. He wants to pass whatever test this ship represents, including the literal test of the shot.
minds.feels: A mixture of quiet awe and a low, private unease he has no language for yet. The 'save the world' mandate is too large to hold, and Cypher's revelation lands on the raw spot of that uncertainty — reframing destiny as a body count. He is being initiated, and initiation here tastes like engine-degreaser and mortality.
minds.shows: He plays the willing initiate: he toasts, he downs the shot even though 'it almost kills him,' he gulps the second one on his own, and he says 'Thanks... for the drink' as if gratitude is the right currency. But the tells leak — he goes 'red-faced,' coughs, looks 'unsure,' and looks 'down at his drink' when the prophecy is mocked. His exit line is a retreat, not a triumph.
minds.basis: His eyes 'light up' at the screens (genuine wonder), he nods for the drink and forces it down to keep pace, and his questions ('Really?' 'How many?' 'What happened to them?' 'How?') show him leaning in. But his downward looks and unsureness when 'save the world' is invoked, plus his physical collapse over the alcohol, register that the information is landing harder than his composed 'Thanks' admits.

believes_about.belief: That Cypher is simply the worldly, honest veteran giving him the straight dope over a friendly drink — a trustworthy guide who's letting him in.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo has no reason yet to suspect that this 'initiation' is also a recruitment into treason. He cannot know that the man pouring his drinks is the same man who will later murder crewmates (ev-023); he takes the confiding tone at face value, which is precisely the vulnerability Cypher is exploiting.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's certainty about him is either true or at least honorable — and that being 'the One' is a singular, sacred thing.
believes_about.wrong_because: Cypher hands him the fact that will rattle this: five came before, all dead. Neo's belief in the specialness of his destiny is now seeded with a pattern of corpses, and though the scene ends with him not yet rejecting it, the seed is planted — the uneasy question he carries into the Oracle scene (ev-021) is exactly this one.

connects_back: The Sentinel scare and the freezing, powerless ship (sc-070–072) have left the crew shaken and physically miserable; Cypher's 'why didn't I take the blue pill' is the emotional residue of having just huddled in a frozen cockpit watching mechanized death glide past — the real world has never looked less worth the price of admission.
Cypher's 'startle' and forced bonhomie read as a man manufacturing ease after a brush with terror, needing to reassert control and normalcy through talk and drink.
sets_up: ev-018: Cypher's disillusionment, voiced here as a private gripe to Neo, hardens into the outright betrayal he will commit against the crew.
ev-021: The 'five dead candidates' revelation is the exact doubt Neo carries into his confrontation with the Oracle, where he questions Morpheus's certainty.
ev-023: Cypher's ability to isolate and manipulate a crewmate one-on-one here foreshadows the lethality of his later treachery — he has already practiced turning a crewmate against the mission.
dramatic_function: This is the seduction-and-initiation scene that plants the story's central ideological fault line. Under the cover of a friendly drink, it converts Cypher's private regret into active subversion and converts Neo's awe into seeded doubt, so that the prophecy — until now presented as awe-inspiring — is retrofitted with a body count. It makes the abstract conflict (faith vs. despair) personal and intimate, and it sets both men on the collision course that will end in Cypher's betrayal and Neo's test at the Oracle.
